summary: Joined node2's and node3's separate segments (attached via node1's eth1 and eth2) into a single transparent L2 domain by building a kernel bridge (br0) on node1 (SONiC) spanning eth1/eth2, after neutralizing docker0's class-E IP leak and masking interfaces-config.service to prevent reconciliation conflicts. Assigned static IPs 192.168.50.11/24 (node2) and 192.168.50.12/24 (node3) on the same subnet via NetworkManager (autoconnect enabled for persistence). br0 carries no IP address, confirming node1 forwards frames at L2 rather than routing between the hosts. Verified direct reachability (ping/arping) and correct MAC learning in node1's bridge FDB for both peers. Persisted the bridge across reboot via a new systemd oneshot unit (l2-bridge.service, enabled at boot). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines, restarted node3, node2, and node1 one at a time using each node's native reboot mechanism, confirmed a changed boot_id on every node, and verified full recovery (bridge forwarding state, FDB relearning, SONiC's 9 containers healthy, and end-to-end L2 ping between node2 and node3) after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected topology: node1 (SONiC) eth1/eth2 link to node2/node3 eth1 on two separate unaddressed segments
Cleaned up docker0 class-E IP leak and masked interfaces-config.service on node1 to prevent config reconciliation from clobbering manual interface state
Created br0 bridge on node1 joining eth1 and eth2 with STP disabled; verified both ports reached 'forwarding' state
Assigned static IPs 192.168.50.11/24 and 192.168.50.12/24 to node2/node3 eth1 via nmcli with autoconnect enabled for persistence

Verified direct L2 reachability with ping and arping showing real peer MAC addresses; confirmed br0 has no IPv4 address (pure L2 bridging, not routing); confirmed FDB learning of both peer MACs on their correct ingress ports

Attempted the native SONiC VLAN CLI (config vlan) for persistence; found it inapplicable since eth1/eth2 are unbound virtio NICs absent from the configdb PORT table, so a systemd unit was used instead
Created and enabled systemd unit l2-bridge.service on node1 to rebuild the bridge automatically at boot
Captured pre-restart healthy baseline (boot_id, bridge state, connectivity) on all three nodes
Restarted node3 via native reboot, confirmed changed boot_id, verified eth1 static IP and connectivity to node2 restored
Restarted node2 via native reboot, confirmed changed boot_id, verified eth1 static IP and connectivity to node3 restored

Restarted node1 (SONiC) via native reboot wrapper, confirmed changed boot_id, verified l2-bridge.service auto-activated, br0/eth1/eth2 reached forwarding state, all 9 SONiC containers came up healthy, and FDB relearned both peer MACs with end-to-end ping working
